learning_outcomes.text: The student must be able to transform existing software blocks into a partial solution of the problem statement.
The student can read existing code and/or use its documentation.
The student must develop a software application in which choices must be made independently based on learned principles and imposed requirements.
The software applications must be logically structured, with a view to maintenance and expandability.
The student understands what concurrent computing entails and the problems (race conditions, deadlock, ...) it brings. The student can implement applications that use concurrent computing.

syllabus_topics: Creating custom widgets and the Qt painting mechanism

assessment_methods.method: Advanced Object Oriented Programming: Theory (Written exam)
Advanced Object Oriented Programming: Lab (Practical test)

assessment_rules: The total score is on a scale of 1-20. The 'Advanced Object Oriented Programming: Theory' component is a written exam weighted at 100%. The 'Advanced Object Oriented Programming: Lab' component is a practical test weighted at 100%, where students develop an application on a PC/laptop. For resits, successful partial results for 'Advanced Object Oriented Programming: Theory' and 'Advanced Object Oriented Programming: Lab' can be carried over within the academic year. The lab resit consists of one assignment.
